hadapsar.text: Integrated townships are a visible part of Hadapsar's housing. Magarpatta is a 182-hectare gated community where, per Wikipedia, construction began in 2000 and continues as of 2025, with apartment clusters of 5 to 11 floors plus row-house and bungalow clusters; Amanora Park Town is a 400-acre township with an independent sewage management system and a separate power grid. Wikipedia's Hadapsar article adds that Amanora Park Town contains Pune's tallest buildings.

hadapsar.text: Wikipedia lists Hadapsar (Sadesatra Nali) among eleven villages merged into the Pune Municipal Corporation in July 2017. In September 2024 the Maharashtra government asked PMC for its opinion on forming a new municipal corporation for the Hadapsar and Wagholi areas, which drew mixed reactions from residents. After a 1 July 2026 PMC demolition drive that covered Hadapsar and Manjari among seven areas, a PMC deputy commissioner urged people not to buy plots in unauthorized layouts or build illegally in newly merged villages before the PMC Development Plan is approved.

sources.title: Pune: Thousands of Litres of Drinking Water Wasted From Leaking Tank in Hadapsar; Shiv Sena Demands Immediate Repair

hadapsar.text: Punekar News reported on 6 July 2026 that heavy monsoon showers again exposed long-standing waterlogging in Hadapsar, Manjari and Mohammadwadi: residents of Shriram Colony (Kale Borate Nagar) said rainwater has collected every monsoon for 15 years, and severe waterlogging with rainwater entering residential premises and parking areas was reported at places including Sasane Nagar, Handewadi Road and Mohammadwadi Gaothan. On 17 August 2024 The Bridge Chronicle reported that a sudden downpour caused knee-deep waterlogging and that the Hadapsar region was particularly affected.

sources.title: Unexpected Downpour in Pune Leads to Severe Waterlogging Across City
sources.quote: After a ten-day break, heavy rains returned to Pune, causing knee-deep waterlogging in several areas within minutes. The Hadapsar region was particularly affected, with significant flooding reported.

hadapsar.text: Wikipedia describes Hadapsar as a major industrial area with employers such as the Serum Institute of India, Honeywell and Bharat Forge, and with three special economic zones (Magarpatta, Amanora Park Town and SP Infocity). wagholi.text: ANAROCK's Prashant Thakur wrote in Punekar News in January 2018 that Wagholi has been under transformation since 2007 and that, of about 22,000 new residential units launched between 2013 and Q3 2017, more than 80% were launched in 2013-15. As one example, a May 2025 report on a society on Wagholi-Lohgaon Road (80 flats in two seven-storey buildings) says its residents were handed possession in 2018.

sources.title: Pune’s Wagholi - From Industrial Area to Hot Residential Destination
sources.quote: The supply of new residential launches in Wagholi was around 22,000 units between 2013 and Q3 2017. More than 80% of the units were launched during the period 2013-15, after which launches declined significantly.

sources.title: Pune: Wagholi Residents Still Await Basic Facilities Seven Years After Possession, Lift Room Collapse Sparks Safety Fears
sources.quote: Despite being handed possession in 2018, residents say key facilities like lifts have never been operational.

wagholi.text: Wagholi has more than 250 housing societies, according to the director of the Wagholi Housing Societies Association quoted in August 2025. ANAROCK's analysis, published in January 2018, said the micro-market is well known for its affordable housing developments.

wagholi.text: Wikipedia says Wagholi was added to the Pune Municipal Corporation area in 2021, and the Wagholi Housing Societies Association said it was merged on 1 July 2021. ANAROCK noted in 2018 that the housing boom had been helped by Wagholi falling under a Gram Panchayat area, with low registration costs and easy legal procedures. In August 2025 PMC's draft ward structure split Wagholi between the Lohgaon-Wagholi and Kharadi-Wagholi wards.

sources.title: Wagholi, Pune

sources.title: Pune’s Wagholi - From Industrial Area to Hot Residential Destination

sources.title: Pune: Wagholi Split Into Two Wards for PMC Elections, Residents Raise Concerns

PMRDA, after complaints from residents of Wagholi and other fringe areas, said in October 2025 that Assistant Town Planners must now inspect sites physically before it grants construction permission within its jurisdiction.

In June 2026, after PMC began alternate-day supply on 15 June with a 25% cut, residents of Wagholi were among those who reported delayed supply, low pressure and, in some cases, no supply at all.

sources.title: Water Crisis In Pune: 250 Housing Societies Voice Grievances In High Court-Mandated Meeting At PMC
sources.quote: Societies from Wagholi and Kharadi also raised similar grievances.

sources.quote: Wagholi requires 3.7 crore litres of clean water. However, apart from only Wagheshwar Water Supply Plant, which has a capacity of providing only 50 lakh litres of water, Wagholi residents regularly face water problems.

sources.quote: Rest assured, after the water supply work, which will complete in around 7 to 8 months, Lohegaon & Wagholi Residents will get water supply every day.

PMC had identified 201 waterlogging-prone spots across the city.

wagholi.text: ANAROCK's research head wrote in January 2018 that Wagholi had changed from an industrial area into a sought-after residential destination, with growth drivers including affordable projects and proximity to the Kharadi IT hub. sources.title: Pune’s Wagholi - From Industrial Area to Hot Residential Destination

sources.title: Wagholi, Pune

pimple-saudagar.text: Large multi-building housing societies exist in Pimple Saudagar. pimple-saudagar.text: Some Pimple Saudagar society buildings are well over a decade old: Roseland Residency told the Times of India in March 2017 that it began rainwater harvesting in 2009, so at least some of its buildings date from 2009 or earlier. In February 2025 a resident of the Siddhivinayak Ginger society on Kunal Icon Road told Pune Pulse that the area's water problem had persisted for 18 years.

pimple-saudagar.text: Pune Pulse reported on 3 April 2026 that Pimple Saudagar, "known as a fast-developing residential and IT hub", has seen a sharp rise in population over the past few years, with large housing societies, schools and commercial establishments, and that a proposal for its own police station had gone to the state government. The Free Press Journal called it a fast-growing residential and commercial area in September 2024, when PCMC approved widening Kunal Icon Road.

sources.title: Pimple Saudagar Set to Get Its Own Police Station, Proposal Sent to State Government
sources.quote: Pimple Saudagar, known as a fast-developing residential and IT hub, has witnessed a sharp rise in population over the past few years.

sources.quote: It will help alleviate the heavy traffic congestion in this fast-growing residential and commercial area.

pimple-saudagar.text: Wikipedia describes Pimple Saudagar as a neighbourhood in Pimpri-Chinchwad, which is governed by the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC). On 29 September 2025 PCMC gave the Deputy Registrar a list of 1,686 unauthorized constructions in the blue floodline zones of the Pavana, Mula and Indrayani rivers and said such properties should not be sold, bought or registered; its Zone D list (Wakad Gaothan, Pimple Saudagar, Rahatni, Pimple Nilakh) accounted for 391.

sources.quote: D Zone: 391 (Wakad Gaothan, Pimple Saudagar, Rahatni, Pimple Nilakh)

pimple-saudagar.text: According to a May 2025 Pune Pulse report, the Water Resources Department mapped a Blue Line (25-year floodplain) and Red Line (100-year floodplain) for the Pavana, Indrayani and Mula, and construction is strictly prohibited within the Blue Line. The same report says former PCMC standing committee chairperson Seema Sawale alleged that the revised Development Plan shows Survey No. 182 in Pimple Saudagar outside the Blue Line although Irrigation Department maps place it in the floodplain; these are allegations, not findings.

pimple-saudagar.text: PCMC started an alternate-day water supply scheme on 25 November 2019, and the Free Press Journal reported on 7 October 2026 that Pimpri-Chinchwad needs 770 million litres a day but gets 665 MLD, with a further 10% cut planned from 16 October 2026. sources.title: Pimple Saudagar Water Crisis: Roseland Residency Residents Forced to Buy Tanker Water

sources.title: Pimple Saudagar society uses rainwater harvesting to beat water woes

kothrud.text: Wikipedia calls Kothrud one of the earliest and now largest suburbs of Pune. kothrud.text: Wikipedia says the many large educational institutions in Kothrud mean a substantial student population and a proportionate housing, food and service economy. The Times of India noted in March 2025 that, more than a decade earlier, the Guinness Book of World Records had named Kothrud one of the fastest developing suburbs in Asia.

sources.title: Kothrud

kothrud.text: Wikipedia says groundwater is accessible through the year in most parts of Kothrud, thanks largely to the underlying geology and the large unconfined aquifers held in and recharged by the Vetal Tekdi hill complex. Question of Cities reported in April 2024, in connection with a proposed 30-metre link road between Paud Road and Senapati Bapat Road across Vetal Tekdi, that PMC's own reports said further degradation of the land surface was likely to damage the fractured or jointed section of the basalt rock and disturb the continuity of groundwater movement.
